questions.stem: The three states of matter are solid, liquid and gas.

parts.label: a
parts.text: Substances can be changed from one state to another. The box lists some words relating to changes of state. Complete the table by giving the correct word from the box for each change of state. Each word may be used once, more than once, or not at all.

parts.label: b
parts.text: The particles in a solid are closely packed, arranged in a regular pattern and vibrate about a fixed position. Describe the arrangement and movement of the particles in a gas.

questions.stem: Rock salt is a mixture of the soluble salt, sodium chloride, and some insoluble impurities. The diagram shows the first three stages of a method used to obtain pure sodium chloride from rock salt. Stage 1 rock salt crushed Stage2 crushed rock salt added to water Stage 3

parts.label: a
parts.text: Name the pieces of apparatus labelled X, Y and Z

parts.label: b
parts.text: State why the mixture of rock salt and water is warmed and stirred in stage 2.

parts.label: b-ii
parts.text: What is water in stage 2? A a residue B a solute C a solution D a solvent

parts.label: c
parts.text: Explain what happens to the impurities in stage 3.

parts.label: c-ii
parts.text: What is the liquid collected at the end of stage 3? A a residue B a solute C a solution D a solvent

questions.stem: Crude oil is a mixture of hydrocarbons.

parts.label: a
parts.text: The diagram shows a column used in the industrial process to separate crude oil.

parts.label: a-i
parts.text: Name the industrial process used to separate crude oil.

parts.label: a-ii
parts.text: State a use for kerosene and a use for bitumen. bitumen

parts.label: b
parts.text: A molecule of the hydrocarbon eicosane has the formula $ \mathrm{C}_{2 0} \mathrm{H}_{4 2} $

parts.label: b-i
parts.text: Explain which homologous series eicosane belongs to.

parts.label: b-ii
parts.text: Name a catalyst used in the industrial cracking of eicosane.

parts.label: b-iii
parts.text: In a possible reaction for the cracking of eicosane, the products are three molecules of $ \mathrm{C_{4} H_{8}} $ and one molecule of another hydrocarbon. Complete the equation for this reaction. $\mathrm {C} _ {2 0} \mathrm {H} _ {4 2} \rightarrow 3 \mathrm {C} _ {4} \mathrm {H} _ {8} +$

parts.label: c
parts.text: Hydrocarbons can be saturated or unsaturated.

parts.label: c-i
parts.text: Explain what is meant by the term hydrocarbon.

parts.label: c-ii
parts.text: State what is meant by a hydrocarbon being saturated.

parts.label: c-iii
parts.text: Describe a chemical test used to distinguish between unsaturated and saturated hydrocarbons.

parts.label: d
parts.text: The unsaturated hydrocarbon $ \mathrm{C_{4} H_{8}} $ has several isomers. The displayed formula for one of these isomers is $\mathrm {H} - \mathrm {C} - \mathrm {C} - \mathrm {C} = \mathrm {C} - \mathrm {H}$

parts.label: d-i
parts.text: Name this isomer.

parts.label: d-ii
parts.text: Draw the displayed formula of another isomer of $ \mathrm{C_{4} H_{8}} $

questions.stem: (a) (i) Explain what is meant by the term covalent bonding. (ii) Draw a dot and cross diagram to show the bonding in a molecule of ethene, $ \mathrm{C_{2} H_{4}} $ Show only the outer electrons.

parts.label: b
parts.text: Substances A and B are covalently bonded and have simple molecular structures. The table gives the boiling points for substances A and B.

parts.label: b-i
parts.text: Explain why substances with simple molecular structures have low boiling points.

parts.label: b-ii
parts.text: Suggest why the boiling point of B is higher than the boiling point of A.

parts.label: b-iii
parts.text: Substance B has the empirical formula $ \mathrm{C_{2} H_{5}} $ and an $ M_{r} $ value of 58. Determine the molecular formula of substance B.

parts.label: c
parts.text: Substance X is also covalently bonded,but its structure is different from that of A and B. It has a boiling point of $ 2 2 3 0^{\circ} \mathrm{C} $. Explain, in terms of its structure, why X has such a high boiling point.

questions.stem: Hot, molten sulfur reacts with oxygen to form sulfur dioxide gas.

parts.label: a
parts.text: Describe what is seen when a sample of hot, molten sulfur is lowered into a gas jar containing oxygen.

parts.label: b
parts.text: Sulfur dioxide gas is formed during the reaction between dilute hydrochloric acid and sodium sulfite, $ \mathrm{N a_{2} S O_{3}} $ A salt and water are also formed. Write a chemical equation for this reaction.

parts.label: c
parts.text: This apparatus can be used to collect a pure, dry sample of sulfur dioxide gas.

parts.label: c-i
parts.text: Suggest the purpose of the silica gel.

parts.label: c-ii
parts.text: Name the method used in the diagram to collect the sulfur dioxide gas.

parts.label: c-iii
parts.text: State the physical property of sulfur dioxide gas that allows it to be collected in this way.

parts.label: d
parts.text: A sample of sulfur dioxide reacts with water to form an acidic solution.

parts.label: d-i
parts.text: Identify the acid formed.

parts.label: d-ii
parts.text: A few drops of methyl orange indicator are added to this solution. State the colour of the indicator in this solution.

parts.label: d-iii
parts.text: Give the formula of the ion responsible for this colour.

parts.label: d-iv
parts.text: An alkali is then added to neutralise the acid. State the final colour of the indicator.

questions.stem: A student investigates the rate of the reaction between magnesium ribbon and dilute hydrochloric acid. The products are magnesium chloride and hydrogen.

parts.label: a
parts.text: The equation for the reaction is $\mathrm {M g} (\dots \dots \dots) + 2 \mathrm {H C l} (\dots \dots \dots) \rightarrow \mathrm {M g C l} _ {2} (\dots \dots \dots) + \mathrm {H} _ {2} (\dots \dots \dots)$ Complete the equation by adding the state symbols.

parts.label: b
parts.text: The student uses these pieces of apparatus in his experiment. This is his method. clean a strip of magnesium ribbon to remove the oxide layer pour $ 50\mathrm{c m}^{3} $ of 0.5 mol/dm $ ^{3} $ hydrochloric acid into the flask put the clean magnesium ribbon into the flask quickly put the bung into the flask to connect the gas syringe record the volume of gas in the syringe every minute for eight minutes

parts.label: b-i
parts.text: Suggest why the student cleans the magnesium ribbon to remove the oxide layer.

parts.label: b-ii
parts.text: Suggest why the student needs to put the bung into the flask quickly.

parts.label: b-iii
parts.text: Suggest when the student should start the stop watch.

parts.label: c
parts.text: The graph shows the results of the student's experiment.

parts.label: c-i
parts.text: Use the graph to find the volume of gas in the syringe at one minute. Show on the graph how you obtained your answer. $\mathrm {v o l u m e} =$

parts.label: c-ii
parts.text: Use the graph to find the time when the reaction stops. $\mathrm {t i m e} =$

parts.label: c-iii
parts.text: Suggest two possible reasons why the reaction stops.

parts.label: c-iv
parts.text: Explain when the rate of reaction is greatest.

parts.label: d
parts.text: Explain how increasing the concentration of the hydrochloric acid affects the rate of the reaction with magnesium. Refer to the particle collision theory in your answer.

questions.stem: In the Periodic Table, the vertical columns of elements are called groups.

parts.label: a
parts.text: The table gives some information about the first four elements in Group 0.

parts.label: a-i
parts.text: State the relationship between the relative atomic mass and the boiling point of these elements.

parts.label: a-ii
parts.text: State why the elements in Group 0 are unreactive.

parts.label: b
parts.text: The elements in Group 7 of the Periodic Table are called halogens. State why the halogens have similar chemical properties. Refer to electronic configurations in your answer.

parts.label: c
parts.text: The order of reactivity of the halogens can be shown by using displacement reactions.

parts.label: c-i
parts.text: When chlorine is added to sodium bromide solution, chlorine displaces bromine. Write a chemical equation for this reaction.

parts.label: c-ii
parts.text: State the colour of the solution formed in this reaction.

parts.label: c-iii
parts.text: Explain whether or not a reaction takes place when bromine water is added to sodium chloride solution.

parts.label: c-iv
parts.text: The displacement reaction between potassium iodide and chlorine can be represented by the ionic equation $2 \mathrm {I} ^ {-} + \mathrm {C l} _ {2} \rightarrow \mathrm {I} _ {2} + 2 \mathrm {C l} ^ {-}$ Explain why this is described as a redox reaction.

parts.label: d
parts.text: Chlorine reacts with hydrogen to form hydrogen chloride gas.

parts.label: d-i
parts.text: Write the chemical equation for this reaction.

parts.label: d-ii
parts.text: Some methylbenzene is poured into beaker A. Some water is poured into beaker B. Hydrogen chloride gas is dissolved in each liquid. A separate piece of dry blue litmus paper is dipped into each solution. A hydrogen chloride dissolved in methylbenzene B hydrogen chloride dissolved in water Explain what happens to the piece of litmus paper dipped into beaker A the piece of litmus paper dipped into beaker B. beaker A beaker B

questions.stem: The table shows information about the effect of adding sodium hydroxide solution to solutions containing zinc ions, calcium ions or aluminium ions.

parts.label: a
parts.text: A student is provided with a sample of a white solid.

parts.label: a-i
parts.text: The student dissolves some of the white solid in water and then adds a few drops of sodium hydroxide solution. A white precipitate forms. She concludes that the sample contains calcium ions. Explain whether the student's conclusion is valid.

parts.label: a-ii
parts.text: Give a different test to show that the white solid contains calcium ions. test result

parts.label: b
parts.text: A hydrated salt has the formula $ \mathrm{A B_{2}. x H_{2}O} $ A is a positive ion and B is a negative ion. When the hydrated salt is heated, this reaction occurs. $\mathrm {A B} _ {2} \cdot \mathrm {x H} _ {2} \mathrm {O} \rightarrow \mathrm {A B} _ {2} + \mathrm {x H} _ {2} \mathrm {O}$ A scientist heats a sample of the hydrated salt until all the water has been lost. She records the mass of the salt before and after heating. The table shows her results The table shows her results.

parts.label: b-i
parts.text: Describe how the scientist could make sure that all the water has been lost.

parts.label: b-ii
parts.text: Use the scientist's results to find the value of x in $ \mathrm{A B}_{2}. \mathrm{x H}_{2} \mathrm{O} $ $[ M _ {\mathrm {r}} \mathrm {o f} \mathrm {A B} _ {2} = 2 0 8 \quad M _ {\mathrm {r}} \mathrm {o f} \mathrm {H} _ {2} \mathrm {O} = 1 8 ]$

parts.label: c
parts.text: Describe how the scientist could use a solution of the salt to find out if the negative ions are chloride ions.

parts.label: d
parts.text: The test shows that the negative ions are chloride ions.

parts.label: d-i
parts.text: Calculate the relative atomic mass of metal A using the formula and $ M_{r} $ value of the anhydrous salt, $ \mathrm{A B}_{2} $

parts.label: d-ii
parts.text: Identify metal A.

questions.stem: Some metals can be obtained by heating their oxides with carbon.

parts.label: a
parts.text: The diagram shows a blast furnace used to produce iron from iron ore.

parts.label: a-i
parts.text: Give the name of an iron ore.

parts.label: a-ii
parts.text: Explain the role of the hot air in the furnace.

parts.label: a-iii
parts.text: Iron(III) oxide can be reduced by carbon Balance the equation for this reaction. $\mathrm {F e} _ {2} \mathrm {O} _ {3} +$

parts.label: a-iv
parts.text: Limestone is one of the raw materials added to the blast furnace. Explain how limestone removes the impurity, silica $ \mathrm{(S i O_{2})} $ , from the furnace. You may use equations to help your answer.

parts.label: b
parts.text: State why aluminium cannot be produced by heating its oxide with carbon.

parts.label: b-ii
parts.text: Describe how aluminium is extracted from purified aluminium oxide.
